gloss: to come forward; to volunteer; to identify oneself

definitions.gloss: to come forward; to volunteer; to step forward
definitions.explanation: To present oneself voluntarily to take on a task, responsibility, or role.

definitions.gloss: to identify oneself; to reveal one's identity
definitions.explanation: To announce who one is, especially when sought or when identity was previously unknown.

examples.japanese: ボランティアに{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
リーダーに{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る{人|ひと}がいなかった。
examples.english: There was no one who stepped forward to be the leader.

examples.japanese: {危険|きけん}な{任務|にんむ}だと{分|わ}かっていたが、{彼|かれ}は{自|みずか}ら{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
examples.english: He knew it was a dangerous mission, but he came forward of his own accord.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}が{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
{目撃者|もくげきしゃ}が{警察|けいさつ}に{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
examples.english: A witness came forward to the police.

examples.japanese: {匿名|とくめい}で{寄付|きふ}をしていた{人物|じんぶつ}が、ついに{名乗|なの}り{出|で}て{正体|しょうたい}を{明|あ}かした。
examples.english: The person who had been donating anonymously finally came forward and revealed their identity.

notes:
A compound verb combining {名乗|なの}る (to give one's name, to call oneself) and {出|で}る (to come out). The {出|で}る component adds the sense of stepping forward from a group or emerging publicly.

USAGE:
- Often used with に to indicate the role or purpose: ～に{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る (to volunteer for ~)
- {自|みずか}ら{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る emphasizes doing so of one's own initiative
- In sense 2, often involves revealing oneself to authorities or the public

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ボランティアに{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る: to volunteer
- {自|みずか}ら{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る: to come forward of one's own accord
- {警察|けいさつ}に{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る: to turn oneself in to the police
- {候補|こうほ}に{名乗|なの}り{出|で}る: to put oneself forward as a candidate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {志願|しがん}する: to volunteer, apply — more formal; often used for military or official contexts
- {立候補|りっこうほ}する: to run as a candidate — specifically for elections
- {申|もう}し{出|で}る: to offer, propose — broader; can be used for requests and suggestions
- {自首|じしゅ}する: to turn oneself in — specifically to police; stronger than {名乗|なの}り{出|で}る in legal contexts
